question.worked_solution:
First, we expand the parentheses and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}(\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -1)(\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +1) & ={sin}^{2}⁡\theta +\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -1 \\  & ={sin}^{2}⁡\theta -1 \\  & =-(1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use the identity $1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta $ to rewrite the expression on the right-hand side. 

$$
-(1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )=-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta 
$$

Therefore, we conclude that:

$$
(\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -1)(\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +1)=-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta 
$$
